conventions.convention: A record contains finite real data or qualitative observations with declared conditions. Calibration bounds are deterministic declarations; the record supplies no sampling law, independence, likelihood, confidence level or coverage probability. Infinite detector responses are excluded from real-valued comparison quantities.
The action uses SI units, x⁰=ct, metric diag(−1,1,1,1), F₀ᵢ=−Eᵢ/c, Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ, j=(cρ,J), and source coupling +jᵛAᵥ. The field action includes the positive factor c⁻¹.

Field variations are real smooth maps compactly supported in a bounded open chart region; the potential and prescribed current are smooth on a neighbourhood of its closure. Particle variations are fixed-endpoint C² variations of a future timelike curve on a nondegenerate compact interval, with a prescribed external C² potential.

The field-action sector inherits Countable Choice; the finite-interval Riemann particle sector is choice-free. Stationarity is adopted without minimality, existence, uniqueness or coupled particle-field solvability.
For ω>0, real fields are encoded by componentwise Re(phasor·e^(−iωt)). Source-free phasors obey div Ẽ=div B̃=0, curl Ẽ=iωB̃ and curl B̃=−iωc⁻²Ẽ.

PEC existence and uniqueness assume the full Axiom of Choice, a bounded smooth stationary obstacle and connected exterior. The outgoing modal condition applies to the scattered electric correction; the total field need not be outgoing.

The ideal dipole fields are prescribed leading transverse radiation fields on punctured space, not exact finite-radius Maxwell solutions. Complex vector norms are Hermitian. The incident amplitude is nonzero, while the dipole amplitude may vanish; actual-source fidelity retains the second-derivative moment mismatch M as well as D and Γ errors.

The scalar aperture datum is a finite complex measure supported on a nonempty compact planar set inside the closed radius-a ball, read in volts. Observations use x₃>0, k=ω/c and I=|u|²/2; I is a squared-field comparison without absolute radiometric calibration or exact Maxwell identification.
Fraunhofer estimates include r=2a and are uniform in direction. Fresnel estimates use a declared fixed range (a+b)/z≤η₀<1. Relative intensity-error statements require u≠0.

The nonlinear weak-field family is assumed only on a common open interval containing zero, with uniform O(η²) position and velocity remainders on compact subsets. Periodic preparation concerns the unique global harmonic extension of the first-order response, not overlap-only periodicity or global existence of the nonlinear family.

load_bearing.statement: On a nonempty bounded open chart region U with compact closure and smooth A,j on an open neighbourhood N, the field action is S[A]=c⁻¹∫U[−FμνFμν/(4μ₀)+jᵛAᵥ]dλ, with F=dA and real compactly supported smooth variations. The separate particle functional is −mc∫aᵇ√(−η(Ẋ,Ẋ))ds+q∫aᵇAμ(X)Ẋμds for a C² future timelike curve, prescribed C² potential, m>0 and fixed-endpoint C² variations. These are finite functionals; no stationarity or existence is asserted.

Defines primary sources with reading limits, real-valued comparison quantities and measurands with actual well-definedness hypotheses, apparatus descriptions, finite data and qualitative observations, declared calibration bounds, uncertainty records, analysis assumptions and qualified interpretations. It asserts no measurement, calibration correctness, sampling law, precision, coverage or empirical truth; missing report detail stays missing.

For ω>0, n≥1 and w∈Cⁿ, zₚ(t)=Re(−wω⁻²e^(−iωt)) is a smooth T-periodic solution of z″=Re(we^(−iωt)), T=2π/ω. Every C² solution on a nonempty open interval is uniquely zₚ+a+bt and has that unique global harmonic-ODE extension. The extension is T-periodic iff b=0, equivalently its derivative at a specified point equals zₚ′ there. Its period mean is a+b(t+T/2); a local periodicity condition with no pair t,t+T is vacuous.

Under Countable Choice, adopt a finite complex measure α supported on a nonempty compact planar aperture S⊂{y₃=0, |y|≤a}, a>0, and ω>0, k=ω/c. For x₃>0 set u(x)=∫e^(ik|x−y|)/(4π|x−y|)dα(y), U=Re(ue^(−iωt)), and model squared field |u|²/2. This is an adopted polarization-insensitive scalar approximation, not a deduction from Maxwell or material closure and not an identification with exact screen traces.

For ω>0 and p₀∈C³ define E_d(x,t)=Re[−μ₀ω² n×(n×p₀)e^(i(kr−ωt))/(4πr)] and B_d=n×E_d/c on r=|x|>0, n=x/r, k=ω/c. These prescribed leading transverse fields include no independent magnetic dipole, higher multipoles or near-zone field; finite-radius Maxwell validity and an actual source are not asserted.

Under the declared ideal harmonic dipole model and Countable Choice, for a nonzero transverse incident plane-wave amplitude e and ω>0, the model cross sections are dσ/dΩ(n)=ω⁴|n×p₀|²/(16π²ε₀²c⁴|e|²) and σ=ω⁴|p₀|²/(6πε₀²c⁴|e|²). Actual compact smooth conserved sources are compared using H(u,r)=Γ_E/r²+μ₀[D(u)+M(u)]/(4πr), with M=|p_act″−p_h″|, and the stated magnetic bounds. Moment matching is an additional condition, realizable over finite windows without an eternal harmonic compact-time source.

For the adopted finite-measure scalar aperture model, u is smooth and Helmholtz off S. Uniformly for r≥2a, its Fraunhofer field error is at most ‖α‖TV(πr)⁻¹[a/r+ka²/r]. On the declared Fresnel range, the proof gives error at most ‖α‖TV(4πz)⁻¹[(a+b)²/(2z²)+k(a+b)⁴/(8z³)]. The period mean of U² is I=|u|²/2, and a field error δ gives intensity error at most δ(|u|+|u_approx|)/2. Exact Maxwell screen data and empirical readings are excluded.

Under Countable Choice and the smooth finite-region action hypotheses, stationarity under every real compactly supported smooth variation is equivalent to ∂μFμν=−μ₀jν on U. For potential-represented fields, commuting mixed partials supplies the cyclic identity, and the four smooth laboratory Maxwell equations follow. No existence, boundary, decay, weak or singular-source branch is asserted.

For the smooth finite-region action and χ∈C_c∞(U;R), the gauge difference is c⁻¹∫Ujμ∂μχdλ=−c⁻¹∫U(∂μjμ)χdλ, with unchanged F and no boundary term. Invariance under every such compact gauge is equivalent to smooth current conservation. For distributional currents only the corresponding pairing equivalence is asserted, retaining smooth current whenever S itself is used.

concerns.concern: The well-definedness paragraph at line 54 says both Ẽ and B̃ are smooth exactly when 'their six real coordinate maps' Re Ẽ_k and Im Ẽ_k are smooth. It lists only Ẽ's coordinates. The explanatory sentence should also include B̃'s six real coordinates; clauses (a) and (b) already require both fields to be smooth.

Fact F3 defines M_h as the supremum over supp α and is used in the direct error estimates. The model permits α=0, whose support is empty, but this fact states no empty-supremum convention and the local proof does not separate that branch. The theorem remains immediately recoverable: all fields and errors vanish for α=0, as the opened kernel supplier explicitly observes in Proof 2.2.

seams_checked.note: The comparison theorem states the supplier's open-domain, unit-direction, C¹, positive derivative-margin and declared-error hypotheses in F6, then applies its n=1 case on the translated parameter interval. The conclusion remains deterministic, without statistical coverage.

The validity remark retains the adopted inertial-rest and causal-memory branches, their own hypotheses and the finite-band qualification. It does not derive unrestricted material response from vacuum Maxwell.
The validity remark preserves prescribed-source scope, nonzero-charge self-energy divergence, the zero-charge exception and the absence of defined singular self-interaction or back-reaction.

The comparison theorem preserves the signed averaged plane-wave flux before explicitly adopting its magnitude convention. The fringe example uses both electric and magnetic amplitudes and retains positive full energy at its electric zero; no sampling claim is imported.

The tensor equation retains the −μ₀jν sign and fixed dictionary. Maxwell variation explicitly restricts the pointwise component equivalence to open U. Particle coupling preserves the prescribed external-field, m>0, constant-charge and timelike hypotheses when importing coordinate force and power.

The Thomson theorem reproduces the relativistic momentum equation and low-speed bound, uses δ=1/2 only after establishing uniformly small velocity, and supplies its own integrated first-variation argument. It imports no trajectory approximation or emitted-field conclusion.

PEC is explicitly adopted as an ideal boundary model with vanishing interior fields, rather than claimed as a finite-conductivity limit proved by material closure. Scalar aperture diffraction is separately adopted and is not inferred from interface or constitutive results.

Actual-source comparisons retain compact smooth conserved sources, source-time windows, r≥2a, fixed retarded time, Countable Choice and the exact D and Γ bounds. The consumer adds the independent harmonic-moment mismatch M; its matched realization is tapered outside a finite window.
